events.title: The election of Clement V
events.shortBlurb: The choice of a French archbishop who would settle the papacy at Avignon began the Church's long exile from Rome…
body: On 5 June 1305, after an eleven-month conclave at Perugia following the death of Benedict XI, the cardinals chose Bertrand de Got, Archbishop of Bordeaux, who took the name Clement V. Not a cardinal and not present at his own election, he was crowned at Lyon that November and never entered Italy as pope.

In 1309 he fixed his residence at Avignon, on lands of the Angevin counts of Provence, beginning the seventy years during which the popes reigned from France. Closely watched by King Philip IV, he summoned the Council of Vienne in 1311, and there in 1312 he decreed the suppression of the Knights Templar, whose order the king had arrested and accused.

Clement died at Roquemaure in April 1314, within months of the king and of the Templar master he had abandoned to the flames. The Avignon residence he had begun endured until Gregory XI returned the curia to Rome in 1377 — an exile that gravely weakened the Church's freedom and prepared the way for the Western Schism.
